subject: Latency spike impacting Atlas Analytics — investigation & next steps
messages:
From: Carlos Martinez <carlos@atlas-analytics.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Production latency spike - Atlas embeddings API (p95/p99 jumps)

Hi Lauren,

We're seeing a sharp jump in inference latency starting ~08:50 UTC — p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.1s and p99 to ~2.8s. Error rate for /v1/embeddings rose to 3.4% synchronous with latency. Our traces and a traceroute are attached for your team to inspect. This is affecting our real-time ranking pipeline and causing ~30% backlog increase.

Can you confirm if anything changed on your side (deploy, routing, config) around 08:45–09:00 UTC? Our traceroutes from eu-west show an unexpected hop to a us-east edge before returning to an EU inference pool which aligns with the RTT bump.

Attachments: atlas-traces-20270408.jsonl, traceroute-atlas-20270408.txt

We can jump on a call if helpful — we're available now.

Thanks,
Carlos Martinez
Sr. SRE, Atlas Analytics

Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 10:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production latency spike - Atlas embeddings API (p95/p99 jumps)

Thanks for the ping — I'm on it. Initial triage notes: traceroute attached by customer shows an extra inter-region hop via eqx-us-east-1 before returning to eu-west-1 pool. I pulled edge flow logs and our route snapshots and found a BGP policy change applied to eu-edge-03 at 08:41 UTC that prefers a transit via our global exchange (us-front-door) for a subset of prefixes.

Evidence summary:
- edge logs (eu-edge-03): "BGP: imported route preference updated - policy id 0x7a3c" at 2027-04-08T08:41:08Z
- observed path shift in our telemetry coincident with p95 jump: eu-edge-03 -> us-front-door -> eu-ingest-02
- customer traceroute shows ~200ms added RTT consistent with transatlantic leg

I've opened INFRA-3421 and attached eu-edge-bgp-change.log and a sample flow dump. Rolling back the policy to the previous preference takes 2–3 min; I'm coordinating the rollback with Network Ops now.

Next steps (immediate):
1) Roll back policy on eu-edge-03 (in progress)
2) Validate p95/p99 and error rate after rollback (monitor dashboards)
3) If rollback fixes, escalate to change-review to ensure policy tests include region-locality checks.

I'll update here as soon as rollback completes.

--
Dylan Brooks
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 08:20:00 +0000
Subject: Root cause & mitigation: EU edge BGP policy rollback completed

Update / summary (post-rollback):
- Timeline: policy change applied to eu-edge-03 at 2027-04-08T08:41:08Z -> rollback initiated 2027-04-08T10:05:12Z -> policy fully reverted 2027-04-08T10:08:40Z.
- Impact: p95 for embeddings in eu-west peaked at ~1.1s and p99 at ~2.8s between 08:50–10:05 UTC; error rate peaked at 3.4%.
- Mitigation: rollback removed the unintended transatlantic egress. By 10:15 UTC p95 dropped back to baseline ~230ms and error rate returned to <0.2%.

Root cause: a change to a global BGP preference (policy id 0x7a3c) was promoted without the region-locality filter in the canary checklist. The policy was meant to affect only internal control-plane prefixes but a regex error in the prefix selector caused live customer prefixes to be matched.

Action items (tracking INFRA-3421):
- Immediate: Add region-locality guarded tests to the BGP promotion pipeline (owner: Network Ops)
- Short-term: Add synthetic canary traffic from EU customers to catch cross-region egress (owner: SRE)
- Postmortem: Draft full postmortem and share with Atlas by EOD Friday.

Customer outreach: Hannah / Lauren — recommended message: acknowledge the incident, summarize root cause (BGP policy promotion bug), outline rollback & metrics, offer a 10% goodwill credit for impacted window and invite them to an exec briefing. If Atlas accepts, I can include the technical slides from the postmortem.

Attachments: eu-edge-bgp-change.log
Related: Grafana link to p95 panel: https://grafana.redwood-internal.com/d/abcd123/atlas-embeddings-prod?panelId=7&from=1680948000000&to=1680955200000

I'll create a formal incident note and the postmortem draft today.
